'''Laure Saint-Raymond''' (born 1975) is a French mathematician, and a professor of mathematics at [[Institut des Hautes Études Scientifiques]] (IHES). She was previously a professor at [[École Normale Supérieure de Lyon]]. She is known for her work in [[partial differential equations]], and in particular for her contributions to the mathematically rigorous study of the connections between interacting particle systems, the [[Boltzmann equation]], and [[fluid mechanics]]. In 2008 she was awarded the [[European Mathematical Society|European Mathematical Society Prize]], with her citation reading:<ref>{{cite web |title=EMS Prizes and Felix Klein Prize Citations and Prize Winner's Lectures |publisher=5th European Congress of Mathematics |date=July 2008 |location=Amsterdam, The Netherlands |page=10 |url=http://www.5ecm.nl/prizewinnersbook.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090205015010/http://www.5ecm.nl/prizewinnersbook.pdf |archive-date=5 February 2009}}</ref>
{{blockquote|Saint-Raymond is well known for her outstanding results on nonlinear partial differential equations in the dynamics of gases and plasmas and also in fluid dynamics. [...] Saint-Raymond is at the origin of several outstanding and difficult results in the field of nonlinear partial differential equations of mathematical physics. She is one of the most brilliant young mathematicians in her generation.}}

== Biography ==
Laure Saint-Raymond studied in Paris, entering [[École Normale Supérieure]] in 1994. In 1996, she received a Master's degrees in [[plasma physics]] from [[Versailles Saint-Quentin-en-Yvelines University]] and in [[applied mathematics]] from [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]]. In 2000 she finished her Ph.D. in applied mathematics at [[Paris Diderot University]], under the supervision of [[François Golse]].

She worked for two years for the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research]], and was named in 2002 full professor of mathematics at the [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]] at the age of 27. In 2007, she moved to the [[École Normale Supérieure]], and is now professor at the [[École Normale Supérieure de Lyon]]. In 2021, she joined the [[Institut des Hautes Études Scientifiques]] in Bures-sur-Yvette, France as permanent professor, the first woman to hold that position in the history of the Institute.

She is the mother of six children.<ref>{{Cite web |date= |title=Rencontre autour des mathématiques -Université Pierre et Marie CURIE - Sciences et Médecine - UPMC - Paris |url=http://www.upmc.fr/fr/culture/sciences_a_coeur_saison_5/rencontre_autour_des_mathematiques.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160105045220/http://www.upmc.fr/fr/culture/sciences_a_coeur_saison_5/rencontre_autour_des_mathematiques.html |archive-date=2016-01-05 |access-date= |website=www.upmc.fr}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==

Her work has been recognized by many international awards, notably the [[Fermat Prize]] and the [[Bôcher Memorial Prize]]. In 2013, she was elected to the [[French Academy of Sciences]], and in 2014 was an [[list of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited speaker]] at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]].<ref>{{cite web |title=ICM 2014 Invited Speakers |url=http://www.icm2014.org/en/program/scientific/section |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160310061734/http://www.icm2014.org/en/program/scientific/section|archive-date=10 March 2016 |date=4 March 2014}}</ref> A partial list of her awards and honors include:

*2003 : Louis Armand Prize of the [[French Academy of Sciences]]<ref>{{Cite press release|url=http://www.academie-sciences.fr/presse/communique/prixarmand_300903.pdf|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140728202320/http://www.academie-sciences.fr/presse/communique/prixarmand_300903.pdf|url-status=dead|title=Le Prix Louis Armand de l'Académie des sciences remis le 30 septembre 2003 à une jeune et brillante mathématicienne |trans-title=The Louis Armand Prize of the Academy of Sciences awarded on 30 September 2003 to a young and brilliant mathematician |archivedate=28 July 2014 |date=30 September 2003 |agency=Académie des sciences Délégation à l’Information Scientifique et à la Communication}}</ref>
*2004 : [[Peccot Lectures|Claude-Antoine Peccot Award]] of [[Collège de France]]
*2004 : [[Pius XI Medal]] of the [[Pontifical Academy of Sciences]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.casinapioiv.va/content/dam/accademia/pdf/vari/saintraymond_piusximedalbooklet.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211211053432/http://www.casinapioiv.va/content/dam/accademia/pdf/vari/saintraymond_piusximedalbooklet.pdf |archive-date=11 December 2021|title=The Award of the Pius XI Gold Medal |date=2004 |publisher=Pontifica Academia Scientiarum}}</ref>
*2006 : The Best Paper prize of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics|SIAM]] Activity Group on Analysis of PDE<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.siam.org/publicawareness/panews.php?id=969 |title=François Golse and Laure Saint-Raymond named recipients of SIAM's premiering SIAG/APDE Prize |date=20 July 2006 |publisher=[[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]]|access-date=23 July 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151227122806/http://www.siam.org/publicawareness/panews.php?id=969 |archive-date=27 December 2015 |url-status=dead }}</ref> for:
::(with [[François Golse]]) "The Navier-Stokes limit of the Boltzmann equation for bounded collision kernels." Invent. Math. 155 (2004), no. 1, 81–161.
*2006 : Prize of the City of Paris for Young Scientists (joint with [[Isabelle Gallagher]])<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.paris.fr/politiques/Portal.lut?page_id=6524&document_type_id=7&document_id=22849&portlet_id=14785 |title=Deux lauréates ex aequo pour le Prix de la Jeune Scientifique Parisienne |date=20 September 2006 |website=paris.fr |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141110030821/https://www.paris.fr/politiques/Portal.lut?page_id=6524&document_type_id=7&document_id=22849&portlet_id=14785 |archive-date=10 November 2014}}</ref>
*2008 : Prize of the [[European Mathematical Society]]<ref>{{cite journal |url=http://smf4.emath.fr/Publications/Gazette/2009/120/smf_gazette_120_82-84.pdf |journal=La Gazette de la Société Mathématique de France |title=Laure Saint-Raymond reçoit un prix de la Société Mathématiques Européenne |first1=Isabelle |last1=Gallagher |first2=François |last2=Golse |pages=82–84 |date=April 2009 |issue=120 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140725093629/http://smf4.emath.fr/Publications/Gazette/2009/120/smf_gazette_120_82-84.pdf |archive-date=25 July 2014}}</ref>
*2009 : [[Ruth Lyttle Satter Prize in Mathematics]] of the [[American Mathematical Society]]<ref>{{Cite journal |url=https://www.ams.org/notices/200904/rtx090400496p.pdf |publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]] |journal=Notices of the AMS |title=2009 Satter Prize |volume=56 |issue=4 |page=496 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250119134525/https://www.ams.org/notices/200904/rtx090400496p.pdf |archive-date=19 January 2025}}</ref> for:

==Research==
In 2009, her work was summarized by the Satter Prize committee as:
{{blockquote|Her research has focused on the study of problems in [[mathematical physics]], including the [[Boltzmann equation]] and its fluid dynamic limits, the [[Vlasov equation#The Vlasov–Poisson equation|Vlasov-Poisson system]] and its gyrokinetic limit, and problems of rotating fluids coming from [[geophysics]]. Her most striking work concerns the study of the hydrodynamic limits of the [[Boltzmann equation]] in the [[kinetic theory of gases|kinetic theory]] of gases, where she answered part of a question posed by [[David Hilbert|Hilbert]] within the framework of his [[Hilbert's sixth problem|sixth problem]].}}
